document.title: Reagan Message to Rajiv Gandhi circa mid-February 1988
document.authors: President Reagan (via Ambassador John Gunther Dean)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: Reagan thanks Gandhi for advance word of Gorbachev's withdrawal statement and restates the US bottom line: complete, irreversible Soviet withdrawal, Afghan self-determination and refugee return. He dismisses Gandhi's fears of a fundamentalist takeover, claiming the resistance is moderate, and says the Najibullah regime cannot hold power without the Soviet Army.

key_claims: The US saw the Soviets as more serious about withdrawing from Afghanistan than before, after Gorbachev's 8 Feb 1988 statement.
The US bottom line was complete, irreversible Soviet withdrawal in the shortest time, self-determination for the Afghans, and the return of refugees.
The US believed the Najibullah regime could not survive without the Soviet Army.
The US discounted the risk of a Khomeini-style fundamentalist regime in Kabul, citing Afghan history, the small Shi'a minority and the moderate resistance.
The US, USSR and Pakistan agreed that any successor government must be the product of Afghans themselves.
The US wanted Soviet participation in an agreement guaranteeing an independent, neutral, non-aligned Afghanistan.
